catalogue: Australian advanced masonry, AAC, stone, earth and render physical objects

objects.name: special-purpose masonry unit
objects.definition: A masonry unit manufactured or cut with geometry intended for a particular corner, edge, opening, bond, service, reinforcement or weathering position rather than an ordinary field position.
functions: Maintain bond or support a detail

cad.pattern: Placed only at scheduled detail positions
cad.placement: Within a masonry course or local subassembly
cad.opening: Profile can reserve grooves, cores or recesses
cad.load: Only as documented for the selected unit

notes: Keep the generic family until a documented unit geometry is selected.

objects.name: face brick
objects.definition: A brick selected so one or more manufactured faces remain visibly exposed as the finished masonry surface.
functions: Carry the selected weathering and appearance evidence
not_synonyms: face shell of a hollow block

cad.pattern: Repeated in a selected bond with exposed faces outward
cad.placement: Visible portions of a masonry leaf
cad.load: Unit role follows the designed wall

notes: Face brick is an exposure and finish role; the actual material can vary and must be scheduled.

objects.name: common brick
objects.definition: A brick intended primarily for masonry that will be concealed, coated or otherwise not selected for a controlled exposed-face appearance.
functions: Receive a selected finish where required

cad.pattern: Repeated in the selected bond
cad.load: Unit role follows the designed wall

notes: Common describes intended finish exposure, not permission to ignore strength, durability or dimensional evidence.

objects.name: masonry closure unit
objects.definition: A shorter or specially shaped unit used to close a bond, complete an end or fit a remaining course length without an uncontrolled fragment.
functions: Complete a wall end or opening return

cad.pattern: Placed at calculated bond closure positions
cad.placement: Wall ends, returns, corners and openings
cad.load: As part of the masonry course

notes: A closure unit must preserve minimum acceptable unit and joint geometry from the selected system.

objects.name: half masonry unit
objects.definition: A manufactured or scheduled masonry unit approximately half the modular length of its matching full unit for maintaining bond at ends, corners and openings.

cad.pattern: Modular half-unit positions derived from the bond
cad.placement: Ends, corners, piers and opening reveals
cad.load: As part of the masonry course

notes: Use the scheduled product dimensions rather than halving a nominal length without considering the mortar joint.

objects.name: corner masonry unit
objects.definition: A unit whose end and face geometry is manufactured or selected to form a finished masonry corner while maintaining the chosen bond and core arrangement.
functions: Form an external or internal corner

cad.pattern: Repeated at each corner course according to bond
cad.opening: Core layout follows the selected unit
cad.load: As part of the wall and any documented reinforced core

objects.name: jamb masonry unit
objects.definition: A special masonry unit used along the vertical side of an opening to form a controlled reveal, frame interface, closed end or reinforced jamb core.
functions: Provide a frame or seal interface
Maintain local reinforcement and bond geometry

cad.pattern: Vertical stack at the opening side
cad.opening: Defines part of the opening reveal

notes: A sash-block groove and a plain closed jamb end are different selectable profiles.

objects.name: masonry sill unit
objects.definition: A sloped, throated or otherwise shaped masonry unit forming the weathering surface and edge below an opening.
functions: Shed water away from an opening
Protect the wall and flashing interface

cad.pattern: Course or selected units across an opening base
cad.opening: Bounds the opening below
cad.load: Self weight and documented imposed actions

notes: Slope and drip geometry are project details, not universal defaults.

objects.name: masonry coping or capping unit
objects.definition: A purpose-shaped unit forming the exposed top of a masonry wall, pier or parapet and directing water away from vulnerable faces and joints.
functions: Protect the top course and wall core

cad.pattern: Continuous top course with controlled joints
cad.placement: Top of wall, parapet or pier
cad.load: Non-structural weathering role unless designed otherwise

notes: Coping can be unit masonry, stone, precast concrete or metal; keep the selected material explicit.

objects.name: bullnose masonry unit
objects.definition: A masonry unit with one or more deliberately rounded exposed arrises for a corner, jamb, sill, pier or wall termination.
functions: Complete decorative or impact-prone masonry details

cad.pattern: Repeated or local according to the detail
cad.placement: Corners, jambs, sills and exposed wall ends

objects.name: splayed masonry unit
objects.definition: A masonry unit with an oblique face or end used to form angled walls, reveals, transitions or decorative profiles without relying on an uncontrolled wedge cut.
functions: Create a splayed reveal or transition
Maintain joint and bond geometry through an angle

cad.pattern: Placed at each scheduled angled transition
cad.placement: Reveals, corners, cants and wall transitions

objects.name: bond-beam masonry unit
objects.definition: A channelled hollow masonry unit that provides a continuous horizontal space for reinforcement and grout to form a bond beam within a masonry wall.
functions: Form permanent sides to a horizontal reinforced core
Receive grout as part of a bond beam

cad.pattern: Continuous scheduled course
cad.opening: Channel is reserved for reinforcement and grout
cad.load: Permanent form unit; structural action belongs to completed reinforced assembly

objects.name: knockout bond-beam block
objects.definition: A hollow concrete masonry block with removable web portions intended to be knocked out in selected courses to create a continuous horizontal reinforcement and grout channel.
functions: Retain grout within the wall course

cad.pattern: Repeated along selected reinforced courses
cad.opening: Web knockout becomes part of the grout channel
cad.load: Part of the completed reinforced masonry

notes: Model the post-knockout channel state separately from the delivered block if construction sequencing is required.

objects.name: masonry lintel unit
objects.definition: A channelled or otherwise special unit used with reinforcement and grout to form a masonry lintel above an opening.
functions: Form the sides and soffit of a reinforced masonry lintel

cad.pattern: Course spanning the opening with scheduled bearing
cad.opening: Forms the opening head
cad.load: Permanent form unit within a designed lintel

objects.name: masonry cleanout unit
objects.definition: A special bottom-course hollow unit with a removable or open face that permits mortar droppings and debris to be cleared before a reinforced core is inspected and grouted.
functions: Provide access to the base of a core
Close to retain grout before filling

cad.pattern: Placed at the base of each scheduled grouted core or cleanout zone
cad.opening: Temporary face opening closes before grouting
cad.load: Part of the grouted wall after closure

notes: Retain open, inspected and closed lifecycle states for construction views.

objects.name: open-end concrete masonry block
objects.definition: A concrete masonry block with one or both end webs omitted so units can be placed around reinforcement or combine adjacent cores into a continuous grouted region.
functions: Reduce obstruction within a reinforced wall

cad.pattern: Placed where reinforcement or continuous grout geometry requires it
cad.opening: Omitted end web enlarges the connected core
cad.load: As part of designed reinforced masonry

objects.name: control-joint masonry unit
objects.definition: A special unit with a rebated, keyed or closed-end profile used beside a designed vertical movement joint while maintaining faces, cores and joint-seal geometry.
functions: Close unit cores beside the joint

cad.pattern: Vertical stacks on one or both sides of a scheduled joint
cad.opening: Shapes but does not fill the joint gap
cad.load: As part of the adjacent wall panels

notes: Do not use control-joint block as an exact synonym for the complete movement-joint assembly.

objects.name: masonry screen block
objects.definition: A perforated or open-pattern masonry unit used in a non-solid screen wall so deliberate voids repeat through the finished assembly.
functions: Create a repeated architectural void pattern

cad.pattern: Repeated manufacturer or project-defined open pattern
cad.opening: Unit perforations remain actual voids

notes: Do not replace the openings with a transparent material; their geometry controls light, air and climbability.

objects.name: running-bond masonry panel
objects.definition: A masonry panel whose successive courses are horizontally offset so vertical joints do not normally align through consecutive courses.
functions: Arrange repeated units into an interlocking bond
Coordinate closures at ends and openings

cad.pattern: Alternating horizontally offset courses
cad.start: Wall end, corner or movement joint
cad.end: Wall end, corner or movement joint
cad.opening: Bond is recalculated around openings
cad.load: Structural role follows the designed wall

notes: The exact offset and closures come from the selected unit module and documented bond.

objects.name: stack-bond masonry panel
objects.definition: A masonry panel in which vertical joints intentionally align through successive courses to create a continuous grid and a different joint and reinforcement arrangement from running bond.

cad.pattern: Vertically aligned perpend joints
cad.placement: Within a specifically designed masonry panel
cad.opening: Aligned module continues or is deliberately reset around openings

notes: Do not generate stack bond by merely zeroing the course offset; reinforcement and restraint inputs differ.

objects.name: header brick course
objects.definition: A brick course in which header faces are exposed and the long dimension of each brick runs into the wall thickness or across adjoining work.
functions: Tie or express brickwork across thickness where designed

cad.pattern: Repeated header-oriented bricks
cad.placement: Scheduled course in solid or bonded brickwork
cad.load: As part of the designed masonry

notes: A header that crosses a drained cavity would bridge it; cavity construction requires the documented detail instead.

objects.name: soldier brick course
objects.definition: A course of bricks stood vertically on end with their narrow long faces commonly exposed, used as an architectural band or opening-head arrangement.
functions: Express an opening head or wall feature

cad.pattern: Vertical bricks repeated along the course
cad.placement: Wall band or above an opening
cad.opening: Can form the visible opening head but needs documented support
cad.load: Not a lintel solely because of its appearance

notes: Keep the concealed lintel or reinforced support separate from the visible soldier course.

objects.name: brick-on-edge course
objects.definition: A course in which bricks are laid on their narrow bed so the larger face is upright, often forming a sill, coping, band or special edge detail.
functions: Create a sill or capping profile

cad.pattern: Bricks laid on edge in a continuous or local run
cad.placement: Sill, wall top, band or detail
cad.load: As documented for the local detail

notes: Australian drawings commonly use brick-on-edge; retain rowlock only as non-preferred search language.

objects.name: reinforced masonry bond beam
objects.definition: A horizontal reinforced and grouted member formed within channelled masonry units so it ties, spans or distributes actions through a masonry wall as designed.
functions: Span or support local masonry where designed

cad.pattern: Continuous or scheduled horizontal reinforced run
cad.opening: Can form a lintel only where designed
cad.load: Structural member according to engineering design

notes: The plugin must not select bar size, grout strength, continuity or support length.

objects.name: reinforced masonry lintel
objects.definition: A horizontal member above an opening formed from masonry lintel or bond-beam units, grout and reinforcement acting together under a documented design.
functions: Continue reinforced masonry around an opening

cad.pattern: Single designed member across an opening
cad.placement: Within the wall above an opening
cad.opening: Spans the opening head

objects.name: grouted masonry core
objects.definition: A connected vertical or horizontal core space in masonry units after it has been filled with specified masonry grout, with reinforcement where scheduled.
functions: Bond reinforcement to the masonry assembly

cad.pattern: Selected connected core routes
cad.end: Bond beam, wall top or termination
cad.opening: Cleanout opening closes before grouting
cad.load: Part of reinforced masonry when designed

notes: A core shown solid is not proof that grout was placed without voids.

objects.name: fully grouted masonry wall
objects.definition: A masonry wall in which all intended connected hollow cores are filled with grout rather than only selected reinforced cells.
functions: Form a comprehensively grouted wall section
Provide documented mass and structural action

cad.pattern: Continuous wall with all scheduled cores grouted
cad.opening: Reinforced and supported as designed

notes: Fully grouted describes extent, not the adequacy of filling or reinforcement.

objects.name: partially grouted masonry wall
objects.definition: A reinforced masonry wall in which grout is placed only in selected cores, bond beams, jambs or other scheduled regions while remaining cores stay empty.
functions: Form a designed reinforced wall economically

cad.pattern: Wall units with explicit scheduled grouted-cell routes
cad.opening: Local grouting follows the opening design

notes: Do not fill every displayed core merely because one reinforcement bar is visible.

objects.name: masonry grout cleanout opening
objects.definition: A temporary access opening at the base of a grouted masonry core or zone through which droppings are removed and the core can be inspected before closure and grouting.

cad.pattern: At bases of scheduled grout zones
cad.opening: Temporary opening is its defining geometry
cad.load: Must be closed as required before completed structural state

notes: Construction and completed views need separate open and closed states.

objects.name: masonry grout stop
objects.definition: A temporary or permanent barrier placed within unit cores or at an end so fluid masonry grout remains within the intended cell, lift or bond-beam region.
functions: Define the end of a grouted region
Prevent unwanted grout loss into adjacent voids

cad.pattern: At ends and boundaries of scheduled grout zones
cad.placement: Inside unit cores or bond-beam channels
cad.load: Fresh-grout containment only unless documented otherwise

objects.name: reinforced masonry pier
objects.definition: A freestanding or engaged pier built from masonry units with scheduled grout and reinforcement so it acts as a designed reinforced masonry support.

cad.pattern: Discrete vertical support
cad.placement: On a designed footing or slab support
cad.opening: Cores follow the selected unit

objects.name: reinforced masonry pilaster
objects.definition: A local thickened vertical masonry projection integrated with a wall and reinforced or grouted to provide a documented support or stiffening role.
functions: Carry a local beam or roof reaction
Concentrate reinforced masonry at a support

cad.pattern: At scheduled support or stiffening locations
cad.placement: Bonded or connected to a reinforced masonry wall

objects.name: masonry reinforcement bar positioner
objects.definition: A small support or clip used inside a hollow masonry core or bond beam to hold reinforcement at its scheduled position during unit laying and grouting.
functions: Maintain bar clearance from unit shells

cad.pattern: Repeated at scheduled support intervals
cad.placement: Inside grouted masonry cores and bond beams

notes: The support product does not itself prove bar cover or final position.

objects.name: built-in masonry connector
objects.definition: A metal or other durable component built into masonry to connect it to another masonry leaf, wall, frame or structural element, excluding the separately classified ordinary wall tie.
functions: Transfer documented actions across an interface

cad.pattern: Repeated only to the approved layout
cad.placement: Built into mortar joints, grouted cores or approved host fixings

notes: Connector geometry and capacity must come from a selected product or engineering detail.

objects.name: built-in masonry anchor
objects.definition: An anchoring component placed into masonry joints, units or grout while the wall is built to provide a future or immediate structural connection.
functions: Remain embedded in the completed wall

cad.pattern: At scheduled connection points
cad.placement: Built into a mortar joint, core or grouted zone

objects.name: wall-to-wall masonry connector
objects.definition: A built-in connector joining an intersecting or abutting masonry wall to another wall where the units are not fully bonded together course by course.

cad.pattern: Repeated vertically at an abutting wall junction

objects.name: masonry cramp
objects.definition: A short shaped metal connector built or fixed into masonry to restrain a stone, unit, wall return or abutting component without acting as ordinary distributed reinforcement.
materials: non-ferrous or protected metal where specified

cad.pattern: At scheduled local restraint points
cad.placement: Within a joint, groove or approved fixing

objects.name: masonry frame cramp
objects.definition: A connector fixed to a door, window or other frame and built into an adjacent masonry joint or core to restrain the frame-to-wall interface.
functions: Keep the frame position coordinated with courses

cad.pattern: Repeated along frame jambs and head as scheduled
cad.placement: Between a frame and masonry reveal
cad.opening: Adjacent to the framed opening

objects.name: sliding masonry anchor
objects.definition: A masonry connector with a slot, channel or sliding engagement that restrains selected directions while allowing documented relative movement in another direction.
functions: Connect masonry to a frame or structure

cad.pattern: Repeated along a moving masonry-to-structure interface
cad.placement: Between masonry and frame, column or slab edge
cad.load: Restrains only documented degrees of freedom

notes: A slotted-looking component does not prove movement capacity unless the installed clearances remain available.

objects.name: remedial masonry wall tie
objects.definition: A post-installed connector used to restore or add restraint between existing masonry leaves or between masonry and backing where original ties are missing, deteriorated or inadequate under an approved repair design.
materials: approved grout or resin where selected

cad.pattern: Post-installed layout from survey and repair design
cad.opening: Requires approved drilled holes

notes: Never infer a safe drilling route through concealed services, reinforcement or membranes.

objects.name: helical masonry tie
objects.definition: A stainless or protected helically formed metal tie installed into masonry joints or drilled paths as part of a documented new-work or remedial restraint system.
functions: Transfer tie action through helical engagement or grout
Connect masonry across a crack or cavity where designed

cad.pattern: Scheduled individual or continuous repair routes
cad.opening: Drilled or raked route remains explicit
cad.load: Only documented tie or crack-stitch role

notes: Helical geometry is a product form, not proof that the installation is a wall tie, crack stitch or lintel repair.

objects.name: masonry bed-joint tying mesh
objects.definition: A manufactured mesh strip laid in mortar bed joints as a tying or accessory component, distinct from structural bed-joint reinforcement designed as reinforcement for masonry.
functions: Tie or reinforce local non-structural masonry details as specified
materials: stainless, galvanized or protected steel mesh

cad.pattern: Continuous strips in selected bed joints
cad.load: Accessory role unless separately designed as structural reinforcement

notes: AS 2699.2 explicitly separates this accessory scope from structural reinforcement in reinforced masonry.

objects.name: masonry shelf angle
objects.definition: A horizontal steel angle fixed to the structure to provide intermittent vertical support to an outer masonry leaf, commonly at floor or frame levels.
functions: Divide tall veneer into supported panels
Transfer vertical reaction into the building structure

cad.pattern: Continuous or segmented horizontal support
cad.placement: At slab edges, beams or structural frame levels beneath masonry
cad.opening: Separate lintel or shelf segment may support openings

notes: Durability evidence and structural design are separate; AS 2699.3 is a durability product standard.

objects.name: masonry shelf-angle bracket
objects.definition: A discrete steel bracket connecting a masonry shelf angle to the main structure while providing the designed stand-off, vertical support and adjustability.
functions: Transfer masonry reaction to the structure

cad.pattern: Repeated at engineered support points

objects.name: masonry shelf-angle anchor
objects.definition: A cast-in or post-installed anchor forming the structural attachment between a shelf-angle bracket or angle and its concrete, steel or masonry support.

cad.pattern: At each designed bracket or angle fixing
cad.opening: Approved drilled hole where post-installed

notes: Host-specific anchor design must not be inferred from bolt appearance.

objects.name: masonry shelf-angle shim
objects.definition: A thin durable plate or packer used between a shelf-angle bracket and its support to establish the documented line, level and bearing condition.

cad.pattern: Local stacks at adjusted support points
cad.placement: Between bracket and structural bearing face

objects.name: masonry cavity closer
objects.definition: A shaped component that closes the exposed edge of a wall cavity at an opening, wall end or junction while preserving required moisture, thermal, fire and drainage functions.
functions: Provide a backing for seals or finishes
Limit moisture, air or pest paths as documented

cad.pattern: Continuous around selected cavity edges
cad.placement: Opening jambs and heads, wall ends and junctions
cad.opening: Bounds a wall opening

notes: A closer must not block required flashing drainage or weep paths.

objects.name: masonry cavity fire-barrier assembly
objects.definition: A tested or assessed assembly installed across a masonry wall cavity at a required line to resist fire and smoke spread while addressing ties, openings, movement and adjacent materials.
functions: Close a cavity at a documented fire-separation line

cad.pattern: Continuous fire-separation line
cad.placement: Across the cavity at documented compartment, floor, opening or roof interfaces
cad.opening: Only tested service treatments may penetrate

notes: Geometry alone cannot establish an FRL; the exact tested or assessed system is required.

objects.name: masonry weephole vent insert
objects.definition: A small manufactured insert placed in an open perpend or formed weephole to preserve an airflow and drainage path while limiting entry of larger pests or debris as its product design permits.
functions: Provide a shaped drainage and ventilation path
Limit selected pest entry without sealing the opening

cad.pattern: At selected open perpends above flashings
cad.opening: Its free passage must remain open

notes: The insert must not replace the actual negative-space weephole object.

objects.name: autoclaved aerated concrete material
objects.definition: A lightweight cementitious material manufactured with a cellular pore structure and cured in an autoclave, used in masonry blocks and factory-reinforced panels or members.
functions: Form lightweight solid units or panels
Provide thermal mass with cellular insulation

cad.placement: Material within an AAC block, panel or member
cad.opening: Cellular pores normally remain material data rather than explicit geometry
cad.load: Only according to the selected AAC system

notes: Do not generate millions of air pores at building scale or use Hebel as the generic canonical name.

objects.name: AAC masonry block
objects.definition: An unreinforced or locally reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete unit laid in courses, commonly with thin-bed adhesive, to form an AAC masonry wall.
functions: Provide a cuttable modular wall unit

cad.pattern: Repeated in thin-jointed courses
cad.load: Unit role according to the selected wall design

notes: Block dimensions and loadbearing limits are selected-product inputs.

objects.name: AAC block masonry wall
objects.definition: A wall assembled from AAC masonry blocks with compatible thin joints, opening supports, movement joints, ties or anchors, moisture controls and surface finishes required by the selected system.
functions: Provide a lightweight solid masonry background

cad.pattern: Bonded courses with system-specific jointing
cad.opening: Uses selected lintels, sills and reinforced jamb details

notes: AAC block masonry and reinforced AAC panel cladding use different unit, joint and support logic.

objects.name: reinforced AAC lintel
objects.definition: A factory-manufactured reinforced AAC member intended to span a documented opening within a compatible AAC wall system.
functions: Support AAC masonry above an opening
Maintain compatible AAC substrate around the opening

cad.pattern: One scheduled member per opening or supported segment
cad.opening: Spans the opening head

notes: Reinforcement orientation and permitted cutting zones must come from the product guide.

objects.name: AAC sill unit
objects.definition: A shaped or cut AAC unit forming the masonry base below an opening and providing the substrate for the selected sill, flashing and finish detail.
functions: Complete AAC masonry below an opening
Form a sloped or shaped sill substrate

cad.pattern: Across the base of an AAC opening
cad.placement: Below a window or other opening
cad.opening: Bounds the opening below

objects.name: AAC U-section unit
objects.definition: A U-shaped AAC unit used as permanent form to a local reinforced and filled horizontal beam, ring beam or opening support within an AAC wall system.
functions: Contain specified grout or concrete infill

cad.pattern: Continuous scheduled course or local member
cad.opening: Channel receives reinforcement and infill
cad.load: Permanent form; completed member role requires design

objects.name: AAC closure unit
objects.definition: A thin, short or otherwise sized AAC unit used to close a course, cover a junction, complete a return or cap a local AAC assembly.

cad.pattern: At scheduled closure positions
cad.placement: Courses, returns, wall ends and junctions
cad.load: As part of the selected AAC assembly

objects.name: AAC thin-bed adhesive
objects.definition: A compatible cementitious adhesive applied in thin joints between AAC blocks or panels instead of ordinary thick masonry mortar in the selected system.
functions: Transfer local actions through the selected system

cad.pattern: Thin continuous beds and perpends where the system requires
cad.load: Joint material within the selected system

notes: Do not thicken a thin-bed joint to ordinary mortar geometry without system approval.

objects.name: AAC patching mortar
objects.definition: A compatible repair material used to fill local chips, service chases, fixing recesses or surface damage in AAC before the selected finish is applied.
functions: Fill approved minor chases or recesses

cad.pattern: Local repair volumes
cad.placement: Within approved AAC damage or recess

notes: A patch does not restore cut reinforcement or structural capacity without an approved repair.

objects.name: AAC panel reinforcement cage
objects.definition: A factory-positioned protected steel mesh or cage embedded through a reinforced AAC panel or member to provide its designed reinforcement.
functions: Transfer actions to bearings or fixings
Control documented cracking and handling actions

cad.pattern: Factory-defined internal reinforcement
cad.placement: Inside a reinforced AAC panel or member
cad.opening: Penetrations must avoid or address reinforcement as approved

notes: Never route a penetration from the visible panel outline without reinforcement location evidence.

objects.name: reinforced AAC floor panel
objects.definition: A factory-reinforced AAC panel designed to span between floor supports as part of a complete structural floor system.
functions: Contribute documented fire, thermal and acoustic performance

cad.pattern: Parallel scheduled panels
cad.opening: Only approved penetrations and trimmers

objects.name: reinforced AAC roof panel
objects.definition: A factory-reinforced AAC panel designed to span between roof supports beneath the complete weatherproof roof build-up.
functions: Contribute documented fire, thermal and acoustic performance

cad.pattern: Parallel scheduled roof panels
cad.opening: Only approved roof penetrations

notes: The AAC panel is not the external waterproof roof covering.

objects.name: reinforced AAC stair tread
objects.definition: A factory-reinforced AAC unit manufactured as a stair tread or step member for a documented compatible stair assembly.
not_synonyms: AAC block used as a step

cad.pattern: Repeated at stair rise and going

objects.name: AAC movement-joint assembly
objects.definition: A deliberate gap and compatible edge, backing and seal components that divide AAC work into panels or separate it from dissimilar structure so documented movement can occur.
functions: Maintain weather, air or fire continuity through a selected joint system

cad.pattern: Continuous scheduled separation line
cad.placement: Within AAC work or at dissimilar interfaces
cad.opening: The movement gap remains real negative geometry
cad.load: No load transfer except through documented joint components

notes: Joint purpose and connector freedom must be explicit; manufacturer use of control and articulation terminology is not universal.

objects.name: stone masonry construction system
objects.definition: A wall or facade system built from natural or manufactured stone units or panels together with mortar, joints, ties, anchors, supports, flashings and movement details appropriate to its construction method.
functions: Form structural or non-structural stone construction

cad.pattern: System-specific stone layout
cad.placement: On or attached to designed structure
cad.opening: Supported and flashed as documented
cad.load: Structural role depends on the selected system

notes: Select solid, tied veneer, adhered veneer or anchored facade before generating parts.

objects.name: natural stone masonry unit
objects.definition: A piece of naturally occurring stone selected, split, sawn or dressed for use as an individual unit in wall masonry.
functions: Provide natural material mass and face
Transfer actions through beds, joints and supports

cad.pattern: Coursed or uncoursed according to the stonework layout
cad.placement: Within a stone wall or veneer
cad.load: Unit role follows the selected system

notes: Natural bedding direction and individual stone variation may be fabrication data rather than a generic texture.

objects.name: manufactured stone masonry unit
objects.definition: A factory-made cementitious, aggregate or composite unit shaped and coloured to provide a stone-like masonry face and installed by a documented masonry or veneer system.
functions: Form repeated wall or veneer geometry
Receive system-specific mortar, anchors or adhesive

cad.pattern: Product-defined repeat with corner and closure pieces
cad.placement: Within solid, veneer or adhered work as approved

notes: Manufactured does not mean adhered; thickness and fixing method determine the system.

objects.name: solid stone masonry wall
objects.definition: A substantial wall built from natural or manufactured stone masonry through its thickness, with mortar, bonds, ties, openings, damp-proofing and supports appropriate to the design.
functions: Form a loadbearing or non-loadbearing solid wall

cad.pattern: Coursed or uncoursed solid stonework
cad.opening: Stone lintels, arches or other designed supports

objects.name: tied stone veneer wall
objects.definition: A single outer leaf of stone units laid in mortar and restrained to a separate structural frame or backing with ties while supported vertically on a footing, ledge or shelf system.
functions: Drain incidental moisture through the cavity

cad.pattern: Mortared stone leaf with repeated ties
cad.placement: Outside a structural backing with a drained cavity
cad.opening: Lintelled, flashed and drained
cad.load: Self-weight supported below; face loads through ties

objects.name: adhered stone veneer system
objects.definition: A thin natural or manufactured stone finish bonded to a prepared backing with a documented adhesive or mortar system rather than standing as a separately supported tied masonry leaf.
functions: Transfer self-weight and face actions through the adhesive system

cad.pattern: Product or project-defined piece layout
cad.placement: Bonded to an approved prepared backing
cad.opening: Returns and terminations follow the selected system
cad.load: Non-structural finish unless explicitly designed otherwise

notes: AS 3958 may apply only where the selected stone product and installation fall within its scope; do not assume every stone facade is tiling.

objects.name: anchored stone facade system
objects.definition: A facade of discrete stone panels or slabs mechanically supported and restrained by brackets, anchors, dowels or cramps attached to a structural backing.
functions: Transfer self-weight and face loads to structure

cad.pattern: Panel grid with individually scheduled supports and restraints
cad.opening: Panels, joints and supports coordinate around openings
cad.load: Facade support system under engineered design

notes: Every panel needs support and restraint identities; do not hang the facade from visual contact alone.

objects.name: stone facade panel
objects.definition: A scheduled slab or panel of natural or manufactured stone prepared with edges, holes, kerfs or inserts for an anchored facade system.
functions: Transfer face actions to restraint anchors

cad.pattern: Scheduled facade panel grid
cad.opening: Fabricated holes and kerfs remain explicit

objects.name: ashlar stone masonry panel
objects.definition: Stone masonry made from accurately dressed units laid in regular courses with controlled bed and perpend joints.
functions: Use dressed bearing and face surfaces

cad.pattern: Regular dressed units in aligned or broken courses
cad.opening: Dressed jamb, sill and head units
cad.load: Role follows the host stone system

notes: Ashlar describes dressing and layout, not a unique rock type.

objects.name: rubble stone masonry wall
objects.definition: Stone masonry using irregular, roughly dressed or undressed stones arranged and packed into a bonded wall or veneer with mortar and smaller packing pieces as specified.
functions: Create a bonded mass through stones, ties and mortar

cad.pattern: Irregular packed and bonded stone layout
cad.opening: Supported with designed stone or separate members

notes: Do not populate a wall by random collision packing; bond, bearings and face control need construction logic.

objects.name: stone quoin
objects.definition: A dressed or selected corner stone forming part of the bonded corner and often visually distinguished from the adjoining wall stones.
functions: Form and strengthen a stone corner
Establish wall lines and course heights

cad.pattern: Alternating or scheduled corner stones
cad.load: As part of the host wall

objects.name: stone sill
objects.definition: A shaped stone member below an opening with fall, projection and drip geometry intended to shed water clear of the wall face and protect the opening interface.
functions: Provide a durable bearing or finish below the frame

cad.pattern: One or more scheduled sill pieces
cad.opening: Bounds the opening below

objects.name: stone lintel
objects.definition: A single or assembled stone member designed to span across a wall opening and transfer supported stonework to the jamb bearings.

cad.pattern: Single member or documented segmented assembly
cad.opening: Spans the opening head

notes: Natural stone bending capacity and hidden reinforcement cannot be guessed from appearance.

objects.name: stone coping
objects.definition: A continuous run of shaped stone pieces capping the exposed top of a wall or parapet with falls, projections and drips appropriate to the weathering detail.

cad.pattern: Jointed continuous run
cad.placement: Top of stone or masonry wall
cad.load: Weathering member; other roles require design

objects.name: stone masonry arch
objects.definition: A curved arrangement of wedge-shaped or carefully jointed stones that spans an opening by transferring compression to its supports and any documented restraint.

cad.pattern: Radial wedge units around an arch curve
cad.opening: Defines the curved opening head

notes: A visually arched joint pattern may still conceal a separate lintel; structural mechanism must be explicit.

objects.name: stone arch voussoir
objects.definition: An individual wedge-shaped or radially jointed stone unit forming part of the ring of a masonry arch.
functions: Transfer compression between adjacent arch units
Create the intrados and extrados geometry

cad.pattern: Radial sequence around the arch

objects.name: stone arch keystone
objects.definition: The central or crown voussoir of a masonry arch, often specially shaped or expressed, but structurally meaningful only as part of the complete arch ring and supports.
functions: Complete the arch ring at the crown

cad.pattern: One or documented crown group
cad.load: Part of compression arch if the arch is structural

objects.name: stone veneer wall tie
objects.definition: A tie selected for the thickness, geometry and jointing of a mortared stone veneer leaf and connecting it to the structural backing for face-load restraint.

cad.pattern: Repeated at documented stone joint locations

notes: Stone joint heights and unit sizes can require a different tie layout from modular brickwork.

objects.name: stone facade support bracket
objects.definition: A discrete metal support attached to structure and shaped to carry the self-weight of one or more stone facade panels through a bearing, pin, dowel or kerf engagement.

cad.pattern: At engineered bearing points
cad.placement: Between structural backing and stone panel

objects.name: stone facade restraint anchor
objects.definition: A metal component connecting a stone panel to backing primarily to restrain face movement and transfer wind actions while allowing the movement intended by the facade design.
functions: Maintain panel position while accommodating selected movement

cad.pattern: At engineered panel restraint points
cad.placement: Between panel edge or back and structural backing

notes: Support and restraint functions may be combined in one proprietary anchor but remain separate roles.

objects.name: stone facade dowel
objects.definition: A short metal pin engaging a drilled hole or compatible insert in stone to locate, support or restrain a panel as part of an engineered facade fixing.
functions: Locate adjoining panel edges where designed

cad.pattern: At scheduled panel edges or backs
cad.placement: Between bracket or anchor and a drilled stone hole
cad.opening: Requires a fabricated panel hole

objects.name: stone panel anchor kerf
objects.definition: A narrow fabricated slot cut into a stone panel edge or back to receive a compatible support or restraint plate as part of an engineered fixing.
functions: Locate the panel relative to its support

cad.pattern: Individual fabricated slots
cad.placement: Edge or back of a stone facade panel
cad.opening: The kerf is explicit negative geometry

notes: Do not cut a kerf automatically where a bracket visually intersects the stone.

objects.name: stone bedding mortar
objects.definition: Mortar selected to form load-bearing beds and filled joints beneath or between stone masonry units while accommodating the stone and wall system requirements.

cad.pattern: Beds and filled joints beneath scheduled stones

objects.name: stone pointing mortar
objects.definition: Mortar placed and finished in the exposed outer portion of a stone joint to protect the joint and provide the specified face profile and appearance.
functions: Provide a replaceable weathering joint face where detailed

cad.pattern: Exposed face strips along stone joints
cad.placement: Outer portion of bed and perpend joints

notes: Repointing must be compatible with the original stone and mortar; harder is not automatically better.

objects.name: stonework movement-joint assembly
objects.definition: A deliberate gap and compatible backing, seal and edge treatment dividing stone masonry or facade panels so documented movement can occur without uncontrolled contact.
functions: Maintain weather or air sealing through a replaceable joint

cad.pattern: Continuous scheduled separation line
cad.placement: Between stone wall or facade panels
cad.opening: Joint gap remains negative geometry
cad.load: No transfer except documented joint components

objects.name: earth wall construction system
objects.definition: A wall system whose principal solid material is selected earth formed as units or compacted monolithically, together with supports, moisture controls, reinforcement, openings, joints and finishes required by its documented design.
functions: Form an earth-based enclosure or internal mass wall
Coordinate earth material with structure and moisture protection
Support the selected openings and finishes

cad.pattern: Method-specific unit courses or compacted lifts
cad.opening: Supported and weathered by documented details

notes: Earth construction is outside the Housing Provisions masonry prescriptive unit list and needs a project-specific lawful pathway.

objects.name: building earth mixture
objects.definition: A selected blend of clay, silt, sand, gravel and water, with fibre or stabilising binder where specified, prepared to form mud bricks, rammed earth or an earth finish.
functions: Bind particles through clay and optional stabilisation
Form units, compacted lifts or finishes

cad.placement: Within an earth unit, wall lift, mortar or finish
cad.load: Material role according to tested mix and wall design

notes: Visible colour cannot establish soil composition, stabiliser content or performance.

objects.name: mud brick
objects.definition: An unfired earth unit made by placing a moist earth mixture, commonly with fibres, into a mould and drying it before laying in a wall.
functions: Create a repairable low-fired-energy wall material
materials: straw or other fibre where selected

cad.pattern: Repeated in courses with earth-compatible mortar
cad.load: Unit role according to project design

notes: Adobe is retained as a regional search synonym; mud brick is the common Australian term.

objects.name: mud-brick wall
objects.definition: A wall constructed from dried mud bricks laid in earth-compatible mortar with designed supports, openings, moisture protection, reinforcement and surface treatment.
materials: reinforcement and bond beams where selected

cad.pattern: Coursed mud-brick masonry
cad.placement: On a raised and moisture-protected designed support
cad.opening: Supported by documented lintels, arches or frames

objects.name: compressed earth block
objects.definition: An earth masonry unit formed by mechanically compressing a prepared earth mixture in a mould, with no assumption that a cement or lime stabiliser is present.
functions: Use mechanical compaction to shape the unit

cad.pattern: Repeated in courses using the selected unit profile
cad.load: According to product and project evidence

notes: Compression method and stabilisation are independent attributes.

objects.name: stabilised compressed earth block
objects.definition: A compressed earth block whose prepared mixture includes a documented stabilising binder such as cement or lime to modify strength or moisture resistance.

cad.pattern: Repeated in documented courses
cad.load: According to tested unit and project design

notes: Stabilised is a material fact, not a visual style.

objects.name: earth or mud mortar
objects.definition: A workable earth-based jointing mixture used to bed and bond compatible mud bricks or earth blocks, with sand, fibre or stabiliser as specified.
functions: Remain compatible with the selected earth units

cad.pattern: Beds and perpends between earth units
cad.load: Jointing role according to wall design

objects.name: earth-building fibre addition
objects.definition: Short straw or another selected fibre mixed through mud brick, cob, earth mortar or render to limit handling cracks and provide the documented material role.
functions: Contribute tensile fibre within an earth mix

cad.pattern: Distributed through the earth mixture
cad.placement: Within earth units, mortar or render

notes: Store as material data at ordinary model scale.

objects.name: rammed-earth wall
objects.definition: A monolithic wall formed by compacting successive layers of a damp earth mixture between temporary forms, then removing the forms to expose or finish the wall.
functions: Create visible compacted lift texture where selected

cad.pattern: Monolithic wall divided into real form and lift placements
cad.opening: Boxed and supported by documented details

notes: Compaction lifts can be visible strata but are not separate masonry courses.

objects.name: rammed-earth compacted lift
objects.definition: One compacted horizontal layer of prepared earth placed within formwork during rammed-earth construction, identifiable by its placement extent and interface with adjacent lifts.

cad.pattern: Successive compacted horizontal strata
cad.load: Part of monolithic wall after compaction

notes: Model lift boundaries only where coordination, construction sequence or visual strata matter.

objects.name: stabilised rammed-earth wall
objects.definition: A rammed-earth wall whose documented mixture includes cement, lime or another stabiliser to modify its strength, erosion resistance or moisture behaviour.
functions: Form a stabilised monolithic earth wall

cad.pattern: Successive stabilised compacted lifts
cad.opening: Documented support and boxing

notes: Stabiliser presence and amount must be recorded; appearance is not evidence.

objects.name: rammed-earth wall formwork assembly
objects.definition: A temporary two-sided mould, end stops, walers, ties, props and supports that contains earth during placement and repeated compaction of a rammed-earth wall section.
functions: Support openings and ends during placement

cad.pattern: Repeated or relocated form bays
cad.placement: Both faces and ends of a wall placement
cad.opening: Includes boxes for documented openings

notes: Rammed-earth compaction forces and form design are not inferred from concrete formwork proportions.

objects.name: earth-wall masonry plinth
objects.definition: A raised durable base of concrete, stone or masonry that supports an earth wall above adjacent ground and splash exposure while coordinating its damp-proof or capillary break.
functions: Raise earth material above ground moisture
Transfer wall load to the foundation

cad.pattern: Continuous support beneath earth walls

notes: Plinth height and moisture detailing are project inputs, not universal values.

objects.name: earth slurry wall finish
objects.definition: A thin brushed or hand-applied earth-rich slurry used to even, colour or repair the surface of compatible mud-brick or earth construction while retaining vapour-compatible behaviour.
functions: Provide a renewable compatible colour layer

cad.pattern: Continuous thin surface film
cad.opening: Stops at openings and movement joints

objects.name: earth render
objects.definition: A thicker trowelled or floated plaster made principally from compatible earth, sand and fibre, applied to an earth or other suitable substrate as one or more coats.
functions: Carry a selected texture and colour

cad.pattern: Continuous coat fields divided at real joints
cad.opening: Returns and stops are explicit

notes: Compatibility and moisture behaviour matter; do not replace with a hard cement render by default.

objects.name: earth-wall protective sealer film
objects.definition: A selected clear or pigmented film applied to an earth wall surface to reduce dusting or erosion while maintaining the moisture behaviour required by the system.
functions: Retain the intended visible earth finish
not_synonyms: structural stabiliser in the earth mix

cad.pattern: Continuous surface film
cad.opening: Stops at openings and joints

notes: A sealer cannot compensate for missing eaves, plinth, DPC or drainage detailing.

objects.name: solid render system
objects.definition: A site-applied plaster or render build-up on a solid substrate, including preparation, bond treatment, base and finish coats, reinforcement, beads, joints and compatible final coating where selected.
functions: Level and protect a solid wall surface
Provide a finish substrate or exposed finish
Coordinate corners, stops, joints and openings

cad.pattern: Continuous coat fields divided at real substrate and movement joints
cad.opening: Reveals, heads and sills are separately returned and beaded
cad.load: Finish system only unless separately engineered

notes: Withdrawn HB 161 is terminology history only; current project specifications and selected products must control.

objects.name: cement-lime-sand render
objects.definition: A site-mixed or supplied render whose principal binder system uses cement and building lime with graded sand and water for compatible solid backgrounds.
functions: Receive or provide the selected finish

cad.pattern: Continuous coat field

notes: Mix proportions must come from current project evidence, not this ontology.

objects.name: lime render
objects.definition: A render in which lime is the principal binder, selected for a compatible substrate and exposure and often used where lower stiffness and vapour permeability are required.
functions: Accommodate selected historic or earth substrates

cad.pattern: Continuous compatible coat fields
cad.placement: On prepared masonry, earth or historic solid backgrounds as specified

notes: Lime render and limewash are different thickness and material states.

objects.name: polymer-modified masonry render
objects.definition: A proprietary cementitious or mineral render containing polymer modification to provide the selected adhesion, flexibility, water or handling properties for a documented substrate and system.

cad.pattern: Continuous manufacturer-defined coat field

notes: Polymer modified is not a universal performance class; retain selected-product evidence.

objects.name: render substrate preparation layer
objects.definition: A cleaned, repaired, roughened, primed or otherwise treated physical surface layer prepared to receive a render system with the required suction and bond condition.
functions: Create the selected mechanical or chemical bond
materials: primer or bonding treatment where selected

cad.pattern: Continuous or local prepared surface fields

notes: Preparation can include operations, but the accepted object is the resulting physical interface or retained treatment.

objects.name: render dubbing coat
objects.definition: A local preliminary render fill used to reduce deep hollows and gross substrate variation before the regular base coat is applied.
functions: Reduce excessive render thickness in later coats

cad.pattern: Local fill volumes
cad.placement: In substrate hollows below regular coats

objects.name: render splatter bond coat
objects.definition: A rough discontinuous or textured first treatment applied to a smooth or high-suction background to create the documented key and suction condition for later render coats.
functions: Condition substrate suction as part of the system

cad.pattern: Rough keyed field over selected substrate
cad.placement: Between prepared substrate and base render

notes: A decorative texture coat and a hidden bond coat have different roles.

objects.name: render base coat
objects.definition: The principal underlying render layer applied over the prepared background to build thickness, cover mesh or lath and provide a suitable surface for subsequent coats.

cad.pattern: Continuous coat field
cad.placement: Over preparation and behind finish coats
cad.opening: Returns and reveals are explicit

objects.name: render float coat
objects.definition: A ruled and floated render layer used to establish the required plane, curve or texture before a thinner set, texture or coating finish is applied.
functions: Provide a keyed or floated finish

cad.pattern: Continuous ruled coat field

notes: Float describes the formed physical layer here; the floating operation remains process data.

objects.name: render finish coat
objects.definition: The outermost trowelled, floated or textured render coat providing the exposed surface or the immediate substrate for a compatible decorative coating.
functions: Provide the final render texture and plane
Receive paint or remain exposed as selected
materials: fine cementitious, lime, mineral or polymer-modified render

cad.pattern: Continuous outer render fields
cad.opening: Returns stop at documented edges

notes: A render finish contains aggregate and binder as a plaster layer; a later texture coating is a separate coating system.

objects.name: render reinforcing mesh
objects.definition: An alkali-resistant or otherwise compatible mesh embedded within a render coat at full fields, stress points or dissimilar-substrate junctions according to the selected system.
functions: Bridge compatible local transitions as specified

cad.pattern: Full fields or local strips with controlled laps
cad.opening: Cut and reinforced around openings as documented

notes: Mesh does not replace a required structural movement joint.

objects.name: render expanded-metal lath
objects.definition: An expanded or formed metal mesh mechanically fixed over a substrate to provide a keyed carrier for solid plaster or render where direct bond is not the selected method.
functions: Carry render across suitable framed or local backgrounds

cad.pattern: Fixed sheets or rolls with supported laps
cad.opening: Trimmed and reinforced around openings

objects.name: render lath fastener
objects.definition: A corrosion-compatible nail, screw, staple, clip or washer assembly fixing render lath securely to its documented support.
functions: Transfer wet render and service actions
Hold laps and edges in position

cad.pattern: Repeated at supports, laps and lath edges

objects.name: render corner bead
objects.definition: A perforated or keyed profile fixed at an external render corner to establish and protect the finished arris while becoming embedded in the render build-up.

cad.pattern: Continuous along an external render arris

objects.name: render casing or stop bead
objects.definition: A keyed profile that provides a straight controlled termination to a render field at an opening, material change, exposed edge or other boundary.
functions: Provide an edge for sealant or adjacent work

cad.pattern: Continuous along render termination lines
cad.placement: At openings, edges and material changes
cad.opening: Commonly frames reveals and openings

objects.name: render movement-joint bead
objects.definition: A paired or flexible profile embedded at the edges of a render movement joint to form straight protected arrises and preserve the designed separation or flexible zone.

cad.pattern: Continuous along documented movement joints
cad.placement: At both edges or centre of a render separation
cad.opening: Preserves the movement gap

notes: The bead must align with and not bridge the movement joint required in the substrate.

objects.name: render drip bead
objects.definition: A shaped render profile forming a downward projection and break in the underside surface so water sheds clear instead of tracking back across a soffit or wall face.

cad.pattern: Continuous along a weathering edge
cad.placement: Underside edges, heads, soffits or base returns as detailed

notes: Bellcast and drip profiles can differ; use the selected profile geometry.

objects.name: render screed or guide bead
objects.definition: A linear guide embedded in render work to establish the required plane, curve, thickness or division while providing a rule-off edge during application.
functions: Divide large or shaped work into controlled bays

cad.pattern: Linear datums within the render field
cad.placement: On substrate at required plane or curve
cad.load: Application guide and retained edge where specified

notes: Retained metal/PVC beads are physical objects; temporary rules are construction equipment and should use a temporary state.
